fields.label: H1 — 2 lines
fields.value: Rubber That Seals a Building Against Water, Wind and Movement.
fields.note: 10 words · the three things a building envelope actually has to resist, and the third is the one that separates construction from every other sector on this site. Buildings move — thermally, structurally, seasonally — and a seal that cannot take movement fails whatever its material

fields.label: Subhead
paragraphs: Extruded EPDM glazing and weatherseal profiles, cellular expansion joint seals, building-services gaskets and vibration mounts for plant — extruded and moulded to your drawing at our ISO 9001:2015 plant in Nashik. Compounded in-house, so the ozone and UV resistance a facade needs for twenty years is formulated rather than bought in.
leads: Extruded EPDM glazing and weatherseal profiles, cellular expansion joint seals, building-services gaskets and vibration mounts for plant — extruded and moulded to your drawing at our ISO 9001:2015 plant in Nashik.
fields.note: 50 words · the last clause is the sector-specific differentiator. A facade seal fails by ozone cracking and UV embrittlement long before it fails mechanically, and in-house compounding is what lets that be specified rather than assumed — which matters more here than on any other industry page

fields.label: Cards ×6
rows: Structural glazing gaskets, wedge and setting-block sections, weather seals and cellular expansion joint fillers. Corner mouldings vulcanised to the profile so the joint is not a butt splice on site.
Extruded weatherseal profiles, bubble and fin sections, glazing beads and cabinet seals.
Self-adhesive closed-cell tape, upstand and penetration seals, membrane termination tape.

Expansion and movement joint seals in dense and cellular section, sized to the joint’s designed range rather than its installed gap.
fields.note:
The last card carries the sector’s core engineering point. A movement joint is specified by its range — the maximum and minimum gap it will see through a thermal cycle — not by the gap on the day it was measured. A seal sized to the installed gap works until the first summer. Saying so on the page is the detail a facade engineer notices
Compound column matches the homepage governing table throughout, and EPDM leads five of six because facade and roof duty is ozone, UV and water — exactly what EPDM is for and exactly what nitrile is not

sections.title: Compound selection
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → router, from the /products/oil-seals compound selector

fields.label: H2
lines: On a Facade, Ozone Decides Before Temperature Does
fields.value: On a Facade, Ozone Decides Before Temperature Does
fields.note: 8 words · states the sector’s selection rule. Every other industry page routes on medium or temperature; construction routes on weathering, and a compound table that leads with temperature would rank the wrong material first

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: External seals fail by ozone cracking and UV embrittlement, not by reaching a temperature limit. A twenty-year facade seal spends its life between −5 and +65 °C and still perishes, because sunlight and atmospheric ozone attack the polymer backbone. Every compound we mix is available; these are ranked for building duty.
fields.note: 52 words · explains the failure mode rather than asserting the choice, which is what makes the EPDM recommendation credible instead of promotional. The temperature range given is deliberately unremarkable — the point is that the seal fails within it

fields.label: Compound router
rows: The default for anything exposed. Outstanding ozone, UV and water resistance; tested to ISO 1431-1. Never where oil or fuel is present
Structural movement, acoustic and vibration pads
Best damping and flex-fatigue of the eight, which is what a load-bearing pad needs. Protected positions only — poor ozone resistance
Marine and coastal exposure, moderate oil, flame-retardant grades
The compromise where salt air, some oil and a flame-retardant grade are all wanted at once
Plant-room pipework carrying oil, fuel or hydraulic fluid
Generator fuel lines and hydraulic plant. Never on a facade — nitrile has poor ozone resistance and will craze in sunlight
High-temperature services, flue and boiler-room gasketing
Where temperature genuinely governs. Low tear strength, so not for a section that is stretched over a frame
Internal and protected positions only. No exposure, no oil
Aggressive chemistry in effluent or process plant
Rarely justified on a building. Specify on the medium, not the temperature
Rarely a construction duty. Listed because every compound is available
fields.note:
Every range is the homepage compound table, which governs across all fifteen category pages. FKM and AEM carry the continuous figure beneath the peak.
The NBR row is the one that earns trust here — “never on a facade” is a refusal aimed at a real and common error. Nitrile is the cheap default in a lot of Indian sealing supply and it crazes within a season in direct sun. Naming that is worth more than another EPDM sentence
EPDM leads and natural rubber is second, which is the fifth different ranking across the five compound routers written in this run. Four pages, five orders, no house favourite

notes: All eight rows in the DOM at first paint. On /products the same component hides seven of eight compound descriptions from crawlers.

fields.note: 6 words · a heading that promises a refusal, on the page of a supplier trying to win work. On construction that reads as competence rather than weakness, because a specifier has been let down by a supplier who said yes to all four

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: Rubber appears in parts of a building where the product is not really rubber, it is a certified assembly. We would rather tell you now than at qualification.
fields.note: 28 words · one sentence, and the second half is the commercial argument. Every hour spent qualifying a supplier who cannot do the work is an hour both sides lose

fields.label: Boundaries table
rows: A structural product type-tested and load-certified to IRC:83 Section IX, IS 15462 or EN 1337-3. We hold no structural product approval and a bearing sits under a deck.
Plain rubber bearing pads and acoustic isolation pads for non-structural duty, quoted against your load and area

A fire rating is certified against a specific tested assembly by a third-party laboratory to IS 3809, BS 476 or EN 1366. A flame-retardant compound is not a fire rating and we will not let the two be confused.
Flame-retardant neoprene grades where the specification asks for a compound property rather than a tested assembly. Third-party testing arranged on request
Single-ply roofing is a warranted system with installer certification behind it. The warranty is the product.
Closed-cell EPDM tape, upstand and penetration seals, and termination detailing that goes with someone else’s membrane
PVC is not a vulcanised rubber and we do not extrude it — the same reason we decline polyurethane liners and polyurethane hydraulic seals.
Rubber waterstops and construction-joint seals in EPDM or natural rubber, where the specification permits them
fields.note:
The third column is what makes this section commercial rather than merely honest. Each refusal is paired with the adjacent thing Margo genuinely does, so a specifier reading it leaves with a product rather than a rejection. All four alternatives are real and all four are already on this site
The fire row is the one that will be carried over by mistake. Sheet 19’s live sector table names “fire-rated seals” as a construction application in plain text. It must not appear on this page as a capability, and sheet 19’s row should be amended to “flame-retardant grades” at the same time.
Sixth boundary section in six new sheets. Diaphragms refused cycle life, bonded components refused bond strength, lining refused polyurethane and butyl, seals refused polyurethane again, the datasheet refused food contact and a flame rating. On this sector the refusal is structural, which is why it gets a numbered section rather than a paragraph

sections.title: Technical & commercial questions
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → FAQ accordion, six questions · these six are the FAQPage mainEntity, verbatim

fields.label: Q1

lines: Which rubber lasts longest on an external facade?

parts.text: EPDM, and it is not close. External seals fail by ozone cracking and UV embrittlement rather than by reaching a temperature limit, and EPDM resists both better than anything else we mix. Nitrile is the common cheap substitute and it crazes within a season in direct sun. We test ozone resistance to ISO 1431-1 at our NABL partner laboratory and will report it on the compound supplied.

fields.note: 67 words · the extractable answer for this page. It names the compound, the failure mechanism, the wrong answer buyers are offered, and the test — in that order. Naming nitrile as the substitute to avoid is what makes it useful rather than promotional

fields.label: Q2

lines: Do you supply elastomeric bearings for bridges?

parts.text: No. Laminated elastomeric bridge bearings are a structural product, type-tested and load-certified to IRC:83 Section IX, IS 15462 or EN 1337-3, and we hold no structural product approval. We do supply plain rubber bearing pads and acoustic isolation pads for non-structural duty, quoted against your load and area — but if your specification calls up a laminated bearing, we are not your supplier and will say so at enquiry rather than at qualification.

fields.note: 76 words · the most important answer on the page. Bridge bearings are the largest rubber market in Indian construction and the easiest thing on this list to imply. Answering it as a flat no, with the standards named and the adjacent product offered, is the whole argument of section 06 in one FAQ

fields.label: Q3

lines: Can you supply sealing rings for concrete pipes and manholes?

parts.text: Yes. Sealing rings to IS 5382 for water mains, gas mains and sewers, and to EN 681-1 for water supply and drainage pipe joints. Send the pipe standard, the joint type and the ring section — those are on our water and fluid management page, and the same team quotes both.

fields.note: 52 words · routes a real construction enquiry to the page that owns it, without duplicating the content. “The same team quotes both” removes the friction a cross-link would otherwise add

fields.label: Q4

parts.text: No, and the distinction matters. A fire rating is certified against a specific tested assembly by a third-party laboratory to IS 3809, BS 476 or EN 1366 — it belongs to the assembly, not to the rubber. We supply flame-retardant neoprene grades where a specification asks for a compound property, and we will arrange third-party testing on request. We will not describe a flame-retardant compound as a fire-rated seal.
parts.lead: We will not describe a flame-retardant compound as a fire-rated seal.

fields.note: 70 words · the second refusal, and the sentence in bold is the one that protects both parties. Sheet 19’s live copy currently names “fire-rated seals” as a construction application — this answer is what stops that becoming a claim

fields.label: Q5

lines: What is the minimum order for extruded profile on a project?

parts.text: We deal in bulk, and on extruded profile the minimum is quoted per profile against total length rather than as a piece count — a curtain-wall package and a window run are not comparable quantities. Moulded components carry the standard minimum of 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound. Send the section and the metreage with the drawing and we will quote it.

fields.note: 62 words · the bulk position adapted to a sector that buys both ways, matching sheet 18 on extrusion and sheet 38 on lining. Construction is the clearest case for the escape clause in the 2026-09-01 instruction — a project buys metres of profile and pieces of moulding on one purchase order

fields.label: Q6

lines: Can you make a non-standard profile for a facade system?

parts.text: Yes — that is most of what we do on this sector. Dies are cut in-house, so a section drawn for your system is a drawing rather than a compromise, and corner mouldings can be vulcanised to the profile so the joint is not a butt splice on site. Send the section drawing and the annual metreage and we will quote the die with it.

fields.note: 65 words · the qualifying answer for a facade contractor, and the vulcanised-corner detail is the one that separates a component supplier from a stockist. In-house tooling is the differentiator on this sector more than on any other
